title: Biallelic mutations in CYP24A1 or SLC34A1 as a cause of infantile idiopathic hypercalcemia (IIH) with vitamin D hypersensitivity: molecular study of 11 historical IIH cases
authors: Pronicka E, Ciara E, Halat P, Janiec A, Wójcik M, Rowińska E, et al.
population: Adults in Poland diagnosed in infancy (1970s to 1990s) with idiopathic infantile hypercalcaemia attributed to 'hypersensitivity to vitamin D'
funder: This study was supported by projects NSC 2014/15/B/NZ5/03541 (National Science Centre) and CMHI 180/09 (The Children's Memorial Health Institute grant). No statement on the role of the funders was found.
result: Idiopathic infantile hypercalcaemia presents with severe hypercalcaemia, failure to thrive, vomiting, dehydration and nephrocalcinosis; periodic rises in incidence in the UK in the 1950s and in Poland and Germany in the twentieth century followed rickets over-prophylaxis, in Poland with 'periodic' doses of 300,000 units three times a year, when at least 36 affected infants were treated at the authors' centre; some needed several months of hospital treatment. All 11 historical cases carried mutations, 9 in CYP24A1 and 2 in SLC34A1, biallelic in all but one. From the frequency of the recurrent CYP24A1 p.R396W allele, incidence in Poland is estimated at 1 in 32,465 births. The authors suggest molecular testing for both genes in each case of idiopathic hypercalcaemia or hypercalciuria in children and adults.
